title: What is left over when each even number is put in rows of four?
description: Six even numbers are laid out as dots in rows of four and sorted by what is left over, none or two. Numbers with nothing left over are of the form four p, and numbers with two left over are of the form four p plus two. Keeko raises the doubt that forty two fills rows of four because it ends in two like twelve.
teaching_notes: One idea: every even number leaves either nothing or two when put in rows of four, and the dots left over decide its form. Watch for students who decide by the last digit instead of making the rows.

source: Sort 4, 12, 18, 22, 36 and 42 into numbers of the form 4p an
video_script.why: A learner sorts even numbers into the forms four p and four p plus two by making rows of four and seeing what is left.
video_script.substitution: the book's own numbers: four, twelve, eighteen, twenty two, thirty six and forty two
video_script.anchor: dots laid out in rows of four, with the dots left over set apart, as in the book
video_script.wrong_answer: forty two fills rows of four because it ends in two like twelve
video_script.wrong_move: decides by the last digit instead of making rows of four and looking at what is left
video_script.payoff_line: Four, twelve and thirty six are of the form four p. Eighteen, twenty two and forty two are of the form four p plus two.

final_answer.spoken: four, twelve and thirty six are of the form four p, and eighteen, twenty two and forty two are of the form four p plus two

maths_rules: 4 = 4 x 1, 12 = 4 x 3, 36 = 4 x 9: nothing left over, form 4p
doubt: 42 ends in 2 like 12, but 10 rows of 4 make 40 and 2 dots are left over
video_script.design: One idea: make rows of four and look at what is left. Assumes even numbers and multiplication facts of four. Wrong idea: the last digit decides. Dots in rows of four stay on the board and the leftover dots are set apart.

beats.on_screen: title card Rows of Four; six number cards 4, 12, 18, 22, 36, 42 on the board; blank dot rows of four beside them

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the six cards line up
marks.ask: two empty boxes labelled 4p and 4p + 2 appear below the cards

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about even numbers put into rows of four.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Six even numbers are on the board. Can each one fill the rows exactly, or is something left over?

beats.on_screen: the six cards stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: ten dots in rows of four: two full rows and two dots apart; the words 4p and 4p + 2 under the two cases

marks.rows: ten dots make two full rows of four
marks.left: the two dots left over are set apart and called the remainder
marks.forms: the forms four p and four p plus two are written under the two cases

narration: <bookmark mark='rows'/>Put dots in rows of four. Ten dots make two full rows.
<bookmark mark='left'/>The dots left over after the full rows are called the remainder. Here it is two.
<bookmark mark='forms'/>Nothing left over means the form four p. Two left over means the form four p plus two.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the numbers are four, twelve, eighteen, twenty two, thirty six and forty two.

beats.on_screen: To find: sort into the form 4p and the form 4p + 2
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to sort them into the form four p and the form four p plus two.

marks.thirty: thirty six is nine full rows

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step one, make rows of four. Four is four times one.
<bookmark mark='twelve'/>Twelve is four times three. Thirty six is four times nine.
<bookmark mark='thirty'/>These fill the rows exactly with nothing left over, so they are of the form four p.

marks.eighteen: eighteen is four full rows and two dots apart
marks.twentytwo: twenty two is five full rows and two dots apart
marks.fortytwo: forty two is ten full rows and two dots apart

narration: <bookmark mark='eighteen'/>Step two, do the same for the rest. Eighteen is four times four, plus two.
<bookmark mark='twentytwo'/>Twenty two is four times five, plus two. Forty two is four times ten, plus two.
<bookmark mark='fortytwo'/>Each one leaves two dots over, so they are of the form four p plus two.

marks.ans: the answer line is boxed and the cards slide into the two boxes

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Four, twelve and thirty six are of the form four p. Eighteen, twenty two and forty two are of the form four p plus two.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the dot rows
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 42 ends in 2 like 12, struck through; forty two dots form 10 rows of four with 2 dots apart

marks.doubt: the bubble with forty two and twelve appears
marks.rows: forty two dots form ten rows of four with two dots apart

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks forty two fills rows of four because it ends in two like twelve.
<bookmark mark='rows'/>But ten rows of four make forty, and two dots are left over.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The last digit does not decide this. The rows do.
